proof:
Source: step 2 (slice operator) of the parent proof. Notation as in the statement.
1. Continuity of the integrands. Fix x ∈ ℝ^N. The map t ↦ ι(t, x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) is continuous ℝ → ℝ^{N+1}: its coordinates are t and the constants x_j (in Lean, fun_prop proves it). Every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^{N+1}) is smooth (its membership proof contains ContDiff ℝ ∞ ω), hence continuous, and for a fixed tuple w evaluation γ ↦ γ(w) is continuous on covectors (continuous_eval_const). Hence g_{ω,x,w}(t) := ω(ι(t, x))(w) is continuous in t and therefore interval integrable on [0, 1] (Continuous.intervalIntegrable).
2. Choice. Fix N, k. By (SA), choose for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) a test form η_ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) with (F_ω): η_ω(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k) dt for all x, v, and with tsupport η_ω ⊆ {x : ∃ t ∈ [0, 1], ι(t, x) ∈ tsupport ω}.
3. Uniqueness. If θ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) satisfies (F_ω) for all x and v, then θ = η_ω: for every x the covectors θ(x) and η_ω(x) take the same value (the same integral) on every tuple v, so θ(x) = η_ω(x) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext); thus the underlying forms coincide and the test forms are equal (Subtype.ext).
4. Linearity. Define S(ω) := η_ω. (a) Additivity: for ω₁, ω₂ and all x, v, (η_{ω₁} + η_{ω₂})(x)(v) = η_{ω₁}(x)(v) + η_{ω₂}(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 ω₁(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) dt + ∫_0^1 ω₂(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) dt = ∫_0^1 (ω₁(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) + ω₂(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv)) dt (intervalIntegral.integral_add; both integrands are interval integrable by step 1) = ∫_0^1 (ω₁ + ω₂)(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) dt, because test forms and covectors are added pointwise. So η_{ω₁} + η_{ω₂} satisfies (F_{ω₁+ω₂}), and step 3 gives S(ω₁ + ω₂) = S(ω₁) + S(ω₂). (b) Homogeneity: for a ∈ ℝ, (a·η_ω)(x)(v) = a·∫_0^1 ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) dt = ∫_0^1 a·ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) dt (intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul) = ∫_0^1 (a·ω)(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) dt, so step 3 gives S(a·ω) = a·S(ω). Hence S is an ℝ-linear map 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) → 𝒟^k(ℝ^N).
5. Properties (i) and (ii) are the formula (F_ω) and the support inclusion chosen in step 2.
6. Property (iii). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) and c ∈ ℝ satisfy |ω(y)| ≤ c for all y, and fix x ∈ ℝ^N. Take Φ from (R1) for (N, k) and put f(t) := Φ(ω(ι(t, x))) for t ∈ ℝ. f is continuous, being the composite of the continuous linear Φ, the continuous ω and the continuous t ↦ ι(t, x) (step 1). For every v, by (i) and the formula for Φ, S(ω)(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k) dt = ∫_0^1 Φ(ω(ι(t, x)))(v) dt = ∫_0^1 f(t)(v) dt (the integrands agree pointwise). For every t, in particular t ∈ [0, 1], |f(t)| ≤ |ω(ι(t, x))| ≤ c by the bound in (R1) and the hypothesis. So (SE) with dimension N, degree k, α := S(ω)(x), this f and this c gives |S(ω)(x)| ≤ c.
7. Steps 2–6 work for every N and k, which proves the statement. □
key_steps: t ↦ ω(ι(t, x))(w) is continuous (ω smooth, ι(·, x) continuous, evaluation continuous), hence interval integrable on [0, 1].
Choose η_ω from (SA); any test form satisfying the slice formula of ω equals η_ω (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext, Subtype.ext).
S(ω) := η_ω is additive and homogeneous by uniqueness and linearity of interval integrals; (i), (ii) hold by the choice.
(iii): apply (SE) to α = S(ω)(x) and f(t) = Φ(ω(ι(t, x))), continuous with |f(t)| ≤ |ω(ι(t, x))| ≤ c by (R1).
